What is displayed as a result of running the code segment?

options.why: Correct. List indexes start at 1; INSERT shifts later elements right and REMOVE shifts them left.
INSERT and REMOVE also change the list.
INSERT adds a new element; it does not replace one.
AP pseudocode lists start at index 1, not 0.

questions.explanation: After APPEND: [1, 4, 20, 5, 38]. INSERT at 2 and REMOVE at 5 give [1, 67, 4, 20, 38].

questions.stem:
A robot is on a 6-by-6 grid of squares. Rows are numbered 1 to 6 from top to bottom and columns 1 to 6 from left to right. The robot starts in row 3, column 5, facing left. `MOVE_FORWARD()` moves it one square in the direction it faces; `ROTATE_LEFT()` and `ROTATE_RIGHT()` turn it 90 degrees in place.

```text
REPEAT 3 TIMES
{
   MOVE_FORWARD()
   ROTATE_LEFT()
}
```

Where does the robot end, and which way does it face?

options.why: The robot turns in every pass, including the last.
The robot moves forward in each pass.
ROTATE_LEFT turns the robot counterclockwise.
Correct. Trace each move and turn in order.

questions.explanation: Tracing 3 passes of 1 move then ROTATE_LEFT ends at row 4, column 5, facing up.

questions.stem: A program has 4 independent tasks that take 41, 22, 50, 54 seconds. The tasks can run in parallel on two processors, and each task runs entirely on one processor. What is the minimum time to complete all the tasks?

options.why: The longest task cannot run at the same time as all the others on just two processors.
Tasks cannot be split in half, so a perfectly even split is not possible.
Correct. Split the tasks between the processors as evenly as possible; the time is the busier processor's total.
That is the sequential time with one processor.

questions.explanation: The best split puts 91 seconds of work on one processor and 76 on the other, so all tasks finish in 91 seconds (speedup 1.84).

questions.stem:
The following code segment is intended to display the sum of the values in `nums`.

```text
FOR EACH n IN nums
{
   total ← 0
   total ← total + n
}
DISPLAY (total)
```

What is displayed when `nums` is `[6, 15, 13, 17]`, and why?

options.text: 17, because total is reset to 0 on every pass
options.why: Correct. The reset inside the loop discards the earlier values.

options.text: 0, because total is reset after the loop
options.why: The reset happens before the addition in each pass.
total is set back to 0 before each addition.

options.text: 6, because the loop stops after one pass
options.why: FOR EACH visits every element.

questions.explanation: Each pass sets total to 0 and then adds n, so only the last value, 17, remains. Moving `total ← 0` before the loop fixes it.

questions.stem: A network has computers P, Q, R, S, T, U. The direct connections are: P–S, P–U, Q–R, Q–T, Q–U, R–S, S–U. What is the minimum number of connections that must fail for computer Q to be unable to communicate with computer P?

options.why: After that many failures a path still remains.
Correct. Removing 2 well-chosen connections separates Q from P; removing fewer always leaves a path.
Some set of 2 connections already disconnects them.
Not every connection needs to fail.

questions.explanation: Q has 3 connections and P has 2. Checking failures systematically shows that 2 is the fewest that leaves no path between them.
